messages.subject: shared hyper parameter goes to zero
parts:
Hi guy's!

I'm having difficulties understanding why the posterior of the hyperSD in the example below is more or less zero, note that there is no likelihood and if we decrease the number of b's the width of the hyperSD posterior increases.

Can anyone out there explain what's happening?

m <- stan_model(model_code = 
            'parameters {
            real<lower=0> hyperSD;
            real<lower=0> b_a;
            real<lower=0> b_b;
            real<lower=0> b_c;
            real<lower=0> b_d;
            real<lower=0> b_e;
            real<lower=0> b_f;
            real<lower=0> b_g;
            real<lower=0> b_h;
            real<lower=0> b_i;
            real<lower=0> b_j;
            real<lower=0> b_k;
            real<lower=0> b_l;
            }
            model {
                hyperSD~normal(0,1);
                b_a~normal(0.01,hyperSD);  
                b_b~normal(0.01,hyperSD);
                b_c~normal(0.01,hyperSD);
                b_d~normal(0.01,hyperSD);
                b_e~normal(0.01,hyperSD);
                b_f~normal(0.01,hyperSD);
                b_g~normal(0.01,hyperSD);
                b_h~normal(0.01,hyperSD);
                b_i~normal(0.01,hyperSD);
                b_j~normal(0.01,hyperSD);
                b_k~normal(0.01,hyperSD);
                b_l~normal(0.01,hyperSD);
                }')
f <- sampling(m, iter = 1000)

Best regards,
Jökull

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] shared hyper parameter goes to zero
parts:
There is no data in that model.

What's happening is the model log density grows
as hyperSD approaches 0 and each b_a through b_l
approaches 0.01. So most of the posterior mass will
accumulate around where hyperSD is close to 0.

If you are thinking of this as "draw a hyperSD from
normal(0, 1) then draw b_a through b_l that's not
how posterior inference works in Stan (or in BUGS/JAGS).
Instead, we sample from p(hyperSD, ..., b_l).

To get a feeling for what's going on, look at this in
just one dimension of b_a and plot density in two dimensions
and observe the limit as hyperSD -> 0 and b_a -> 0.01.

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] shared hyper parameter goes to zero

Hi Bob,

Could you try setting a lower bound on the b's and plot the hyperSD, and also plot it in the case where there is no lower bound on the b's.

If there is no lower bound, the hyperSD will be more or less half a N(0,1).

But if the there is a lower bound on the b's, the hyperSD gets concentrated around 0.

- Jökull

On Tuesday, October 4, 2016 at 8:20:29 PM UTC+2, Bob Carpenter wrote:
With more variables, the mass gets more concentrated around
hyperSD values near zero.

And by the way, you could do this very easily as

parameters {
  vector[7] b;

model {
  b ~ normal(0.01, hyperSD);

so you don't have to do so much cut and paste.
